office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering the tax structure, school and child-care funding, housing and landlord-tenant law, behavioral-health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: An open seat after 23 years of Democrat Timm Ormsby: Republican teacher Natalie Poulson narrowly led the primary over Democrat Luc Jasmin III, the governors' Eastern Washington liaison. Poulson runs on no new taxes, audits and enforcement-first public safety; Jasmin on child care, education, health care and housing-first services.

candidates.summary: Republican special-education teacher and former Spokane Public Schools employee, running again after losing to Ormsby in 2022, on lower taxes, spending audits, enforcement-first public safety and parental rights.
highlights: Will "stand against any form of state income tax" and wants to repeal or lower the B&O tax [S2][S6]
"Enforcement first": consequences for property crime and public drug use, involuntary treatment, treatment-first over housing-first [S3][S4]
Describes herself as pro-life and supports limits on gender-affirming care for minors [S4]

taxes.basis: Opposes any state income tax and new broad-based taxes and would repeal or lower the B&O tax, in repeated statements.

spending.basis: Repeatedly calls for independent audits, cutting bureaucracy and not renewing programs without results.

housing.basis: "Supply-side solutions, not more spending or mandates": cut permitting delays, fees and state construction mandates, favor market-rate housing.

safety.basis: "Enforcement first," ending catch-and-release, custody or mandatory programs for repeat offenders, involuntary treatment and treatment-first over housing-first.

climate.basis: Opposes natural-gas restrictions in new construction on cost grounds; no broader climate-policy statement.

experience.basis: Never held public office beyond precinct committee officer; runs as a non-politician seeking change after 30 years of the same representation.

local-control.basis: Advocates local control of housing decisions and wants to stop Olympia from piling on construction rules.

immigration.basis: Opposes state suits against federal immigration enforcement and sanctuary incentives; supports cooperation on serious criminals.

social.basis: Pro-life and supports parental consent and limits on irreversible gender-affirming procedures for minors, while respecting current abortion law and adult choice.

parental-rights.basis: Names parental rights as a platform plank (families, not government, make decisions for children) without specific notification or opt-out proposals.

tech.basis: Opposes broad AI regulation as harmful to innovation but would roll back data-center tax exemptions.

candidates.summary: Democratic child-care business owner and Eastern Washington liaison for Governors Inslee and Ferguson, running on cost of living, child care, education, health care and housing.
highlights: Supports a more progressive tax structure but said he would not back further tax increases in his first term [S4][S6]
Backs housing-first approaches, behavioral-health crisis responders and tenant protections against rent hikes [S3][S4]
Supports current protections for gender-affirming care and abortion; endorsed by Gov. Ferguson, the State Labor Council and WEA [S1][S4]

taxes.basis: Supports asking those with the most resources to pay more, but said he will not support further tax increases in his first term.

spending.basis: Opposes closing the budget gap through cuts to schools and behavioral health and proposes more investment in education and health care, while citing reduced administrative waste.

housing.basis: Pairs tenant protections against rent hikes and down-payment assistance with supply measures (missing middle, office conversions, faster building).

safety.basis: Backs housing first, non-police crisis response and harm reduction, with law enforcement focused on trafficking and violent crime and clear expectations on public drug use.

climate.basis: Would condition data-center tax breaks on renewable-energy and water commitments and fund home energy-efficiency upgrades.

experience.basis: Never held legislative office, but runs on four years inside state government as the governors' liaison and his Olympia relationships.

local-control.basis: Says local leaders know the economy better than Olympia in backing Spokane's tax pilot and supports protecting local governments from unfunded mandates.

immigration.basis: Wants the state to act as a firewall so agencies are not tools of punitive immigration crackdowns; lists immigrants' rights as a priority.

social.basis: Supports current gender-affirming-care protections and shield laws and fully supports abortion protections, in questionnaire and campaign site.

tech.basis: Supports impact assessments and audits for high-risk AI, a ban on algorithmic discrimination, data protection and tighter data-center exemptions.
